title: Tanzanian Lamb Stew
community: Popular in coastal Tanzania and for Eid celebrations
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Mchuzi wa Kondoo — Tanzanian lamb stew with coconut milk, Zanzibar spices, tomatoes, and coriander. Rich, aromatic, and deeply satisfying — the celebration lamb stew of coastal Tanzania and a favourite Eid dish.
longDesc: Lamb stew with coconut milk is the celebration version of Tanzanian meat stew — the coconut milk adds richness that elevates lamb beyond the everyday, and the full Zanzibar spice array makes it one of the most aromatic stews in East African cooking.
steps: Cook onions until golden. Add garlic, ginger, spices. Stir 1 minute.
Return lamb. Add water. Simmer covered 60 minutes until tender.
Add coconut milk. Simmer gently 10 minutes.
chefTips: Add coconut milk only after the lamb is tender.
Never boil hard after coconut milk is added.
commonMistakes: Adding coconut milk too early — it over-reduces.
cookingScience: See TZA026 for coconut milk cooking science.
culturalNote: Lamb stew is the Eid meat of Tanzania's Muslim coastal communities — the dish prepared from the sacrificed animal and shared generously with family, neighbours, and the needy.
